correctness.rationale: For normalized a,b>0 the two-update transfer P=M(b)M(a), M(c)=[[1,−c],[1,0]], has trace 1−s, determinant p=ab and characteristic z²−(1−s)z+p. Quadratic Jury gives p<1 and s<2+p. With 0<p≤s²/4, root-radius is strictly decreasing in p to repeated root p=(1−s)²/4 then increasing as sqrt(p), proving piecewise exact optimum and the s=1 unattained infimum. Strict stability is achievable iff 0<s<3 versus equal-rate s<2. At s>.5≠1 the critical pairs are (s±sqrt(2s−1))/2 and N=P−(1−s)I/2 has N²=0, ||N||_F=1+a_first. Singular-value determinant-one calculation yields exact ||P^m||2 and strict smaller-first-rate transient advantage for every m≥1. Independent exact matrix checks covered six critical parameter families, 18 finite-horizon singular norms and the (1/4,9/4) witness. No noisy/nonquadratic/general delay result follows.
